To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new immunofluorescent test (C4/C-3-IFT) can be used to diagnose and monitor the disease activity of polymyalgia rheumatoid arthritis and/or giant cell arteritis.

a new serological reaction, C4/C 3-IFT, is regularly observed with fresh sera of PMR and GCA patients and that this reaction may be used as a sensitive serological marker of disease activity in PMR and G CA patients.

C4/C3-IIFT can be used as a reliable serologic marker in the primary diagnostic of polymyalgia rheumatism and/or giant cell arteritis and secondly that it can be used as sensitive criterion for disease activity in these two diseases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new serological reaction (deposition of C4 and/or C3 components on kidney medulla structures) that is regularly observed with fresh sera of active GCA and PMR patients.
the detection of complement C4/C3 deposition on rat kidney structures in patients with PMR and/or giant cell arteritis (GGA) and the demonstration of its diagnostic value in this disease.
the detection of a new serological reaction (i.e., C4/C3 immunofluorescent test) in patients suffering from PMR and/or temporal arteritis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
C4/C3-IIF is a serological reaction that may be used for the primary diagnosis of GCA and/or active PMR and for the monitoring of disease activity.

C4/C3 deposition in patients with GCA and/or polymyalgia rheumatica can be regarded as a serological reaction which may reflect an activation of the complement cascade, probably via C-reactive protein.
the positive C4/C3 reaction is not a specific serological marker for GCA and PMR but is a sensitive serological marker for an activation of the complement system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
C4/C3 deposition to rat kidney structures is a sensitive serological reaction in PMR and/or giant cell arteritis and is mediated by CRP in patients' sera.
the C4/C3 reaction represents an in-vitro model of the in-vivo complement activation process in patients with inflammatory diseases.
the C4/C3 immunofluorescent test (C4/C4-IFT) is an important serological marker for the diagnosis and follow up of PMR and GCA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C4/C3 immunofluorescent test can be used to monitor disease activity in PMR and GCA patients.
C4/C3 immunofluorescent staining can be a useful tool for diagnosing PMR.
C4/C3-IIF is a reliable serological test in the primary diagnosis and follow-up of patients suffering from PMR/GCA.
